# AGENTS.md

Guidance for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and others) working in this repository. `CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to this file.

## Overview

`iiriix/agent-plugins` is a marketplace of independently installable plugins. Every entry, including one that is just a single skill, is a plugin folder under `plugins/<name>/` laid out per the [Agent Plugins specification](https://agent-plugins.org/specification) (v1.0.0):

```
plugins/<name>/plugin.json                  manifest: $schema, name, version, description, ...
plugins/<name>/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md      Agent Skills format (https://agentskills.io), plus bundled files such as scripts/
plugins/<name>/mcp.json                     MCP servers, if any
```

- The spec defines no marketplace, so `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (Claude Code marketplace `iiriix`) is the catalog: one entry per plugin with `"source": "./plugins/<name>"` and `"strict": false`. Claude Code ignores `plugin.json`, uses the entry as the manifest, and finds the plugin's `skills/` folder on its own, so the entry has no `skills` field. Other tools load a plugin by its folder.
- The spec only covers skills and `mcp.json`. Claude-only components (`agents/`, `commands/`, `hooks/`) work in Claude Code but aren't portable.
- Each skill must work when its own folder is copied elsewhere (that's how OpenCode and `npx skills add` use it), so it can't reference files outside that folder.

`tests/` sits outside `plugins/` so tests don't ship, and mirrors it: repo-wide checks at the top, a plugin's tests in `tests/plugins/test_<name>.py` (module names use underscores; each folder needs an `__init__.py` for unittest). `tests/test_marketplace.py` checks every `plugin.json` against the spec's rules, every `SKILL.md`'s frontmatter, that each plugin has exactly one marketplace entry, and that the entry's `version`, `description` and `license` match `plugin.json`.

## Commands

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests                         # all tests
python3 -m unittest tests.plugins.test_toman_rates.TestRender # one test class
claude plugin validate --strict .                             # marketplace manifest
claude plugin validate --strict plugins/<name>/skills         # one plugin's SKILL.md files
```

## Adding a plugin

1. Create `plugins/<name>/plugin.json` with `"$schema": "https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json"`, `name` (equal to the folder; lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `.`, at most 64 characters), `version` starting at `0.1.0`, `description`, `author`, `homepage`, `repository`, `"license": "MIT"` and `keywords`. The spec's schema is closed: no other top-level fields.
2. Add skills as `plugins/<name>/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md`. The skill `name` must equal its folder (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, at most 64 characters), and `description` (at most 1024 characters) says what it does and when to use it, since that's what the agent matches against. Put scripts in the skill's `scripts/` and refer to them relative to the skill folder; prefer standard-library Python so it runs anywhere. A single-skill plugin usually uses the same name for the plugin and the skill.
3. Add a marketplace entry with the same `name`, `version`, `description` and `license` as `plugin.json`, plus `author`, `homepage`, `repository`, `keywords`, `"source": "./plugins/<name>"` and `"strict": false`.
4. Add `plugins/<name>/README.md` (what it does, how to install it, requirements), tests as `tests/plugins/test_<name>.py`, a row to the root README's table, and a section to `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Releasing

Each plugin is versioned on its own; installs follow `main`, so `main` should always be releasable. There are no git tags or GitHub releases: a release is the version bump landing on `main`. For each plugin that changed, and only those:

1. Bump its `version` (semver) in both `plugin.json` and its `marketplace.json` entry (the tests fail if they differ), or users may not get the update.
2. Add the changes under its section in `CHANGELOG.md`.

## toman-rates

A single-skill plugin. `plugins/toman-rates/skills/toman-rates/scripts/toman_rates.py` is a single-file Python CLI, standard library only, that must keep working on Python 3.8. It gets currency rates in Toman (USD, CAD and EUR by default) from pluggable sources, iran-market.github.io by default, and prints text, JSON or CSV. Keep its `SKILL.md` and README in step: update them when flags, output format, sources, currencies or exit codes change.

```sh
S=plugins/toman-rates/skills/toman-rates/scripts/toman_rates.py
python3 $S                 # text output
python3 $S -o json         # or --output json|csv
python3 $S -c gbp,try      # or --currencies; ALL for every currency
python3 $S -s iran-market  # or --sources; default all registered sources
```

- A source is a function taking no arguments and returning `Rates` (currency code → Toman per single unit, `int`, or `float` when not whole), registered with `@source("name")` into `SOURCES`. Registration order is the default `-s` order and the output order. Fetch with `get()`/`get_json()`, which set the User-Agent, apply the 20s timeout and turn non-200 responses, network errors and bad JSON into `SourceError`.
- Each source returns every currency it has; entries that don't parse are skipped rather than failing the source, and finding no currencies at all is a `SourceError`. `number()` normalises values (positive numbers only; whole floats become `int`). `main` then filters to the `-c` list via `available()`: requested order for a list, sorted for `ALL`. A requested code that no source has is reported to stderr as `no rate for XXX`.
- Private sources and APIs (keyed or paid APIs, internal feeds, anything that stays out of the repo) go in `scripts/private_sources.py` next to the script (gitignored; never commit it). `load_private_sources()`, called at the start of `main`, runs it if present. It registers sources with `@source` via `from toman_rates import ...`, which works when the script runs as `__main__` because the loader first aliases `sys.modules["toman_rates"]` to the running module. A broken private file raises rather than being skipped. Tests don't load it.
- **iran-market**: reads `latest-toman.json` from raw.githubusercontent.com (updated every 30 minutes), `data.categories.currency[]` entries with `currency` `IRT`. Symbols `XXX_IRR_FREE` (`IRAN_MARKET_MAIN_RE`) win over `PRICE_XXX` (`IRAN_MARKET_OTHER_RE`); the crypto tokens in `IRAN_MARKET_NON_CURRENCY` and longer symbols (dollar variants, `DIFF_*` ratios) are ignored. `price` is divided by `unit_size` (JPY is quoted per 100). `stale` entries are kept, since the feed marks rates stale while the market is closed.
- Sources are fetched concurrently, and results keep the `-s` order. A failing source is reported to stderr and skipped. The exit code is 0 if at least one source succeeded and at least one requested currency was found, 1 if no source succeeded, no currency was found or writing stdout failed, and 2 for an invalid `-o`, `-c` or `-s` value (via argparse).
- `render()` returns the whole output as a string, written to stdout in one checked write. Text is a table with a row per currency and a column per source, `-` where a source lacks one. JSON relies on dict insertion order to keep source and currency order stable; keep that if you change the output.

# Toman rates

Gets current free-market rates for foreign currencies in Toman with the bundled script `scripts/toman_rates.py`. The built-in source is `iran-market` ([iran-market.github.io](https://iran-market.github.io), free-market data updated every 30 minutes).

## Run it

The script path is relative to this skill's directory:

```sh
python3 scripts/toman_rates.py
```

With no arguments it prints USD, CAD and EUR from every source. It makes one web request per source and usually finishes in a few seconds (each request times out after 20 seconds).

- `-c`/`--currencies` takes comma-separated ISO 4217 codes, case-insensitive (default `USD,CAD,EUR`). Use it when the user wants other currencies.
- `-c ALL` returns every currency the sources have (over 100). Use it only when the user wants the full list, or to find out whether a currency is available.
- `-s`/`--sources` picks sources by name (default: all of them). `--help` lists them.
- `-o`/`--output` is `text` (the default), `json` or `csv`. Use `json` when you need to compute with the values, for example to convert an amount; use `csv` only when the user asks for it.

## Output

Text is a table with a row per currency and a column per source that succeeded, `-` where a source doesn't carry a currency:

```
Toman   iran-market
USD         103,500
CAD          74,200
EUR         120,300
```

JSON has one object per source that succeeded. Currencies keep the order given to `-c` (alphabetical for `ALL`), and a source that doesn't carry a currency leaves it out:

```json
{
  "iran-market": {
    "USD": 103500,
    "CAD": 74200,
    "EUR": 120300
  }
}
```

Values are Toman per single unit of the currency: whole numbers, or decimals for low-value currencies and those quoted per 100 units (for example JPY). The numbers above are illustrative only; always run the command for real values.

- Multiply by 10 if the user asks for Rial.
- The feed is updated every 30 minutes, and rates stay at the last close while the market is shut (for example on Fridays), so a figure can be a few hours old.

## Exit status and errors

| Exit | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| 0 | At least one source was read and at least one requested currency found. A failed source is reported on stderr as `<source>: error: ...` and left out of the output; a currency no source has is reported as `no rate for XXX` and left out. |
| 1 | No source could be read (`no source could be read`), none of the requested currencies were found (`none of the currencies were found`), or writing output failed. |
| 2 | Invalid `-o` value, currency code (`-c` takes 3-letter codes or `ALL`) or source name. |

If a currency isn't found, tell the user the source doesn't list it. If a source fails, show the stderr message; it's a network call, so a retry may help, but don't loop on it.

## Answering the user

- Say where the numbers came from. If more than one source answered, show each rather than averaging unless asked.
- Format numbers with thousands separators (for example 103,500 Toman).
- Rates change throughout the day; note that the figures are as of when the command ran.

# agent-plugins

Plugins and [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io). Each plugin installs on its own and follows the [Agent Plugins specification](https://agent-plugins.org/specification).

| Plugin | Contains | Description |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| [toman-rates](plugins/toman-rates/) | 1 skill | Live currency rates in Iranian Toman from the free iran-market.github.io feed. |

## Install

Each plugin installs on its own. See its README, linked in the table, for what it does, its requirements and plugin-specific install commands.

**Claude Code:**

```
/plugin marketplace add iiriix/agent-plugins
/plugin install <plugin>@iiriix
```

**Hermes Agent:** install each skill from its folder. Hermes scans it and asks you to confirm (`--yes` skips the prompt), and `hermes skills update` keeps it up to date.

```sh
hermes skills install iiriix/agent-plugins/plugins/<plugin>/skills/<skill>
```

**Other agents (skills):** with the [skills CLI](https://skills.sh), `npx skills add iiriix/agent-plugins` lets you pick which skills to install and for which agents. Or copy a skill's folder (`plugins/<plugin>/skills/<skill>/`) into the agent's skills directory, such as `~/.config/opencode/skills/` for OpenCode.

**Tools that load Agent Plugins:** point them at the plugin's folder, `plugins/<plugin>/`.

## Development

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests                   # all tests, plus checks on every plugin.json, SKILL.md and the marketplace
claude plugin validate --strict .                       # marketplace manifest
claude plugin validate --strict plugins/<name>/skills   # one plugin's skills
```

See [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for how to add a plugin and release a new version, and [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) for changes.

# toman-rates

Live exchange rates in Iranian Toman from the free [iran-market.github.io](https://iran-market.github.io) data feed. Returns USD, CAD and EUR by default, or any of the 140+ currencies it lists.

The plugin has one skill, `toman-rates`. The agent uses it when you ask things like "what's the dollar rate in Toman?" or "convert 500 euros to Rial".

## Install

**Claude Code:**

```
/plugin marketplace add iiriix/agent-plugins
/plugin install toman-rates@iiriix
```

**Hermes Agent:** `hermes skills update toman-rates` keeps it up to date.

```sh
hermes skills install iiriix/agent-plugins/plugins/toman-rates/skills/toman-rates
```

**Other agents:** `npx skills add iiriix/agent-plugins --skill toman-rates`, or copy [`skills/toman-rates/`](skills/toman-rates/) into the agent's skills directory (for OpenCode, `~/.config/opencode/skills/`).

## Requirements

- Python 3.8 or newer (standard library only, nothing to install)
- Network access to raw.githubusercontent.com

## Use the script directly

The skill runs [`skills/toman-rates/scripts/toman_rates.py`](skills/toman-rates/scripts/toman_rates.py), which also works on its own:

```sh
python3 skills/toman-rates/scripts/toman_rates.py                  # USD, CAD and EUR
python3 skills/toman-rates/scripts/toman_rates.py -c gbp,try,aed   # any 3-letter codes, or ALL
python3 skills/toman-rates/scripts/toman_rates.py -o json          # text (default), json or csv
python3 skills/toman-rates/scripts/toman_rates.py -s iran-market   # pick sources (default all)
```

```
Toman   iran-market
USD         271,905
CAD         194,310
EUR         305,360
```

## Adding a source

Sources are pluggable. Add a function to the script that takes no arguments and returns a dict of currency code to Toman per unit, register it with `@source("name")`, and raise `SourceError` if it can't be read. Every registered source runs by default, concurrently, each shown in its own column, and `-s` picks among them:

```python
@source("example")
def example() -> Rates:
    d = get_json("https://example.com/rates.json")  # get()/get_json() raise SourceError on failure
    return {"USD": d["usd"], "EUR": d["eur"]}
```

Check that the source's terms allow this kind of use before adding it.

### Private sources

Private sources and APIs, such as an API that needs your own key or a paid feed, go in `skills/toman-rates/scripts/private_sources.py`. That file is gitignored, and the script loads it if it exists. Write it the same way, importing what it needs from the script:

```python
from toman_rates import Rates, SourceError, get_json, source

@source("example")
def example() -> Rates:
    ...
```

It only takes effect where the file exists, such as your checkout or a skill folder you copied it into. Installs from GitHub never have it.

## Notes on the data

- iran-market.github.io republishes free-market rates as public MIT-licensed JSON, updated every 30 minutes. Rates stay at the last close while the market is shut.
- Values are per single unit: currencies the feed quotes per 100 units (such as JPY) are divided accordingly, and low-value currencies keep their decimals.
